subject: Temporary log hold + secure handoff plan for MediSpring forensics
messages:
From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@medispring.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediSpring Security <security@medispring.com>, Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@legalmedi.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary preservation + secure handoff for fraud investigation

Hi Mateo,

We found a set of anomalous transactions tied to a subset of tenant sessions that started 2028-07-03. Our internal forensics team needs a time-limited retention extension for the last 90 days of request/response logs tied to tenant ID ms-8752 while we complete analysis. Two asks:

1) Can Redwood place a temporary preservation hold for tenant ms-8752 so logs are not rotated/deleted for 90 days (starting now)?
2) If Redwood cannot extend tenant retention in-place, can you provide a secure export (forensics handoff) of the relevant log slice into our S3 bucket under a time-limited, encrypted transfer, plus a deletion certificate once Redwood removes its copies?

Also need: a short description of how PII/PHI will be handled during export (we prefer redaction where possible), a signed attestation of destruction once the investigation closes, and copies of SOC 2 summary + SIG/CAIQ mapping for our security questionnaire.

We'd like to accelerate this (investigation team is on a tight timeline). Please advise required approvals, expected timeline, and any commercial implications (credits/fees).

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Shah
Director of Security
MediSpring Health
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@medispring.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary preservation + secure handoff for fraud investigation

Ben / Karthik / Neha — looping you in to coordinate. Summary from Rajiv: temporary 90-day hold or secure export of tenant ms-8752 logs (request/response, auth traces, and associated metadata). Customer asks for redaction options, destruction attestation, SOC2 & SIG/CAIQ docs, and the timeline and cost.

Initial thoughts / options:
- Option A: Tenant-scoped preservation hold (prevent normal TTL deletion for 90 days). Low operational overhead but requires legal sign-off and a scoped SLA change.
- Option B: One-time export to customer-provided S3 (time-limited role), with a forensics bundle and a Redwood-supplied "proof-of-delete" manifest after we remove retained copies. This is practical and auditable.

Karthik — can our infra produce an export with customer-provided S3 role + KMS encryption, and generate a SHA256 manifest + signed deletion certificate once we scrub our side? Also need confirm whether we can run PII redaction as part of the export (field-level scrubbing or deterministic hashing).

Ben — if we do Option B there may be a one-off operational fee (eg, assisted export + packaging). Please confirm cost estimate or credit offer for an enterprise SOC2 customer.

Neha — legal: we will need a short addendum to the DPA (temporary preservation + export + destruction attestation). Can you flag required language or a quick template?

Attachments I'm preparing: redwood_soc2-summary-2027.pdf (SOC2 high-level), medispring-forensics-bundle-template.zip (sample manifest + packaging), sig-caiq-mapping.csv (controls mapping).

If we can get a go/no-go today we can schedule an export tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@medispring.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary preservation + secure handoff for fraud investigation

Hi all — technical reply / constraints:

1) Preservation hold: we can flag tenant ms-8752 in our retention service to skip normal TTL pruning for up to 120 days. This is a config change that will keep logs in cold storage (no hot cache impact) but we need explicit signed authorization from Legal and a start/end date.

2) Export to customer S3: supported. Process we recommend:
   - Customer provides S3 bucket ARN + IAM role with write-only permissions, or a pre-signed, short-lived upload endpoint (we prefer role assumption with STS).
   - Export will be KMS-encrypted using a customer-managed key or Redwood-managed key (customer key preferred for separation).
   - Redwood will produce a manifest.csv with per-file SHA256 checksums and a manifest.sig (signed by our ops key) so the customer can verify integrity.
   - After export completes, we can run a removal job that emits a signed deletion certificate (time-stamped, includes manifest of deleted object IDs).

3) PII/PHI handling: we have two supported export modes:
   - Raw export: full fidelity logs (recommended only with a customer-managed key and explicit legal ok).
   - Redacted export: apply deterministic hashing for fields matching our PII pattern list (emails, national ids) and remove configurable fields (full user message content). Redaction will be applied at packaging time; redaction rules are configurable but require a short test run to verify.

4) Timing & ops: With approvals + S3 role, a standard export job for the requested 90-day slice can be executed within 24 hours; packaging + signature + deletion certificate within an additional 6 hours. If we also do in-place preservation hold, that's immediate once legal signs off.

5) Audit artifacts: we'll include an operations runbook (export job id, node ids, time windows), the SHA256 manifest, and the signed deletion certificate. SOC 2 summary and SIG/CAIQ mapping are attached for the questionnaire items.

Operational notes: we must log the customer's request in our change control board and create a short-lived change record ID for audit. Also recommend we require the customer to sign a short export acknowledgment form (we can use the template in medispring-forensics-bundle-template.zip).

Happy to proceed on Option B once Legal and Finance sign off.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer (Security & Ops), Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@medispring.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, MediSpring Security <security@medispring.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary preservation + secure handoff for fraud investigation

Rajiv — thanks for the clear ask. Proposed next steps and timeline:

1) Customer action: provide S3 bucket ARN and an IAM role ARN we can assume (write-only) OR provide a pre-signed upload endpoint. Also send a signed export acknowledgment (I attached a fillable template in the related link). Please indicate whether you want raw or redacted export.

2) Legal: Neha will prepare a short DPA addendum for the temporary hold/export and the destruction attestation. Neha — can you target a 4-hour turnaround?

3) Finance/CS: Ben — confirm any one-time assisted-export fee. If MediSpring confirms SOC2 customer status we can apply a 50% professional-services credit to be helpful here.

4) Ops: once (1)-(3) are complete we will schedule the export and aim for completion within 24 hours. Redwood will deliver: medipreserve-<export-id>.zip (KMS encrypted), manifest.csv (SHA256), manifest.sig (signed), and deletion-certificate-<export-id>.json (signed).

For clarity — if you prefer we simply enable a tenant-scoped retention hold instead of export, say so and we'll implement immediately after legal sign-off; that avoids transferring logs but lengthens time Redwood holds them.

If you can reply with the S3 details and whether you want raw vs redacted, we'll queue the job. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
